title: Prove stable joint-bank Gram spectral obstruction (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Prove a scoped obstruction for the complete P104 Gram pair: one persistent Gaussian-dyadic invertible code cannot transform it to the spectral-projector pair with alpha*beta=169, even when the code mixes both banks and any finite number of identically restored dirty scratch coordinates. No new kappa is claimed.

```text
PR3979: bank-separate free spectral normalization excluded
new:    joint-bank codes + arbitrary restored scratch also excluded
        endpoint correction rank >=832; balanced case >=1664
```

The new block calculation gives ranks 1664, 128 and zero for F-I and its next two powers modulo 13. The correction bounds are sharp over F13. Exact dyadic attainment is open. Matrix rank is not a native-call tariff or a complete paid invoice.

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Chris R / Clear1nsight's [PR3979](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3979), at `a8a1d744811cd7d1f9c43ec7ccbae85ef9695b61`, for the tensor-code model and the cited premises A²=13A, n=104 and rank(A mod13)=8. Its original code, invoice and proofs are not replayed or audited. The P104/native/caller lineage keeps its credit. Jordan classification and rank inequalities are classical.

## Evidence

Before, PR3979 explicitly left general bank mixing outside its obstruction. After, the complete-operator invariant excludes every common joint code and finite identity-restored stabilization in the stated ring.

Local CPython 3.12.15 on macOS arm64 passes:

- 20 literal atomic tensor-block cases over five prime fields and 80 small assemblies.
- All 9216 canonical P104 components and all 21632 Jordan coordinates, with an explicit projector-arrow permutation attaining the modular rank-832 correction.
- 75 stable fixtures covering every zero-product coefficient residue pair, plus rational odd-denominator, omitted-stage, unreturned-scratch and invalid-parameter controls.
- Both warning-strict registered commands, timed locally at 0.038 and 0.037 seconds. Their generated hash-bound receipts agree. The complete registered package command passes.
- Exact seven-file publication bytes, modes and declared source ancestry. Official export integrity and input coverage pass. Normal and optimized Git-free replays pass with an empty PATH and eight read-only exported files, including export metadata; bytes and modes remain unchanged.

From the worktree root:


A different CPython 3.12 executable can replace the local interpreter path. Expected markers are `PASS_P104_JOINT_SPECTRAL_OBSTRUCTION modular_repair=832 balanced=1664 no_new_kappa`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.

## Limits and unrun obligations

The quantified claim rests on PROOF.md and the cited Gram premises. Finite canonical-block corroboration is not a reconstruction of the predecessor's original matrix. One common endpoint code, the Gaussian-dyadic ring and identity return of the whole scratch space are essential. Distinct endpoint codes, interleaved new operations and changed targets remain outside the theorem.

No exact dyadic rank-832 correction, native realization, selected caller/compiler/precision/storage/tape/analytic replay, full multiplication theorem, independent human review or formal proof-kernel acceptance is claimed. No registered scientific command is left for CI alone. The selected frontier and frozen packages retain their bytes.

## Open next questions

Can an exact Gaussian-dyadic correction attain rank 832? Begin with the n=2, r=1 integral example A=[[13,1],[0,0]] in the proof, one common dyadic-invertible code and a rank-two correction. A modular solution alone does not lift the endpoint. A physical construction must then price native access and complete restoration.

## Related open work

No open PR was found on this exact two-stage spectral-normalization question. Related work has distinct contracts or quantities:

- [#6166](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6166) studies the P104 ternary decoding code; this proof concerns the complete Gram pair modulo 13.
- [#6173](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6173) studies two-channel support in that code; no support optimum is computed here.
- [#6171](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6171) reduces tensor-frame rank moments under fixed boundaries; it does not identify this dyadic spectral endpoint.
- [#6172](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6172) studies variable-target signed tensor moments in an abstract contact graph; no common invoice or numerical optimum is compared.
- [#6144](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6144) changes P104 owned-word trajectories; this package supplies no word edit or kappa comparison.
- [#6167](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6167) retains an operand to change another P104 root stop; no trajectory or kappa comparison is computed here.
- [#6169](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6169) resynthesizes P104 scalar events; this obstruction supplies no event or scalar-unit saving.
- [#6170](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6170) supplies P104 design tooling; no tool or predecessor checker is changed here.
- [#6175](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6175) localizes ADD-coefficient faults in P104 words; this package studies a different algebraic endpoint invariant.
- [#6178](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6178) bounds costs of functional decoder pairings over fields; its pairing alphabet is not the persistent joint-code contract here.
- [#6180](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6180) certifies rectangular dirty circuits; it does not compute this spectral correction rank.

- [#6183](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6183) studies real contractive approximation of the P104 Gram channel; this exact Gaussian-dyadic conjugacy and correction-rank obstruction computes a different quantity. No approximation optimum is computed here.

The finish-line refresh checked this account's open PRs created since the CLAIM and added #6183 as new related Gram-channel work. The two results compute different quantities, so no numerical agreement or disagreement is asserted. No extra computations were run to validate these other contributions. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19267739). Canonical main remained `3f0152a32eeebac0df11946dbd50cabe5a7f7839` at the submission refresh.
